sections.h2: Who bills property tax on a Waco house?
sections.html:
Waco is in McLennan County, so the McLennan Central Appraisal District sets the value, the taxing units set their rates, and the McLennan County Tax Office bills and collects.

The Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate puts Waco at 147,788 people, 5.5% above the 2020 estimates base, spread over about 88.7 square miles of land. For 2020 to 2024 it reports 49.4% of homes owner-occupied, a median owner-occupied value of $221,700 and a median gross rent of $1,165. With roughly half of homes rented, many Waco owners are landlords, and a landlord's tax bill has no homestead exemption on a rental house.

A Waco address can sit inside several taxing units at once. The county's 2026 rate sheet lists McLennan County, McLennan Community College, a school district and the City of Waco, plus a Waco improvement district at $0.100000. The school unit depends on the address. Besides Waco ISD, the sheet lists Midway, Connally, La Vega, China Spring, Lorena and a dozen other districts, so confirm which one appears on your account.

  • Values, exemptions, protests: McLennan Central Appraisal District, 315 S 26th Street, Waco.
  • Bills and payments: McLennan County Tax Office.
  • City rate and budget: the City of Waco's finance department.

sections.h2: What are the Waco property tax rates for 2026?
sections.html:
The City of Waco's 2026 rate is $0.755000 per $100 of taxable value, split into $0.578371 for operations and $0.176629 for debt service. The city's finance page describes its adopted budget for fiscal year 2026-2027 as maintaining the tax rate at 75.5000 cents.

The finance page also says the average household will see a $73.75 decrease on its property tax bill and will pay an additional $7.97 per year in utility and fee changes, as printed by the city. It lists a total operating budget of $733.3 million. Because the rate is unchanged, any change in your city bill comes from your own taxable value.

sections.h2: When is Waco property tax due?
sections.html:
Taxes are due when the bill arrives and become delinquent after January 31 of the following year. McLennan County says that if January 31 falls on a Saturday or Sunday, the due date moves to the next regular business day.

The state's late schedule applies to Waco accounts. On February 1 the collector adds a 6% penalty and 1% interest, the penalty grows 1% a month until July 1, when it reaches 12%, and interest keeps running at 1% a month with no ceiling. A unit that hires a private attorney can add up to 20% more. Owners 65 or older, disabled owners and disabled veterans may split the bill into four installments, and the state allows penalty and interest to be waived in limited cases when the request is in writing.

  • October: bills go out from the tax office.
  • November 30: the first half is due under the state's split-payment rule, with the second half due the following June 30.
  • January 31: the general due date for the full amount.
  • February 1: penalty and interest begin.

sections.h2: How do I pay McLennan County property tax?
sections.html:
You can pay online with a property tax account number. Ask the tax office about in-person and mail options. The online payment site is run by an outside company, and the county asks you to direct questions about the site to the tax office rather than the county webmaster.

The county lists a 2.19% convenience fee for credit cards and a $1.50 flat fee for an electronic check, both paid to the payment vendor. Credit card payments need only the account number. An electronic check needs the account number and bank details. Visa, Mastercard, Discover and American Express are accepted.

The tax office runs tax sales online through GovEase, and bidders register there. Texas limits redemption rights after a tax sale to certain property types and time windows, so an owner facing a sale should ask the tax office what applies.

sections.h2: How do I lower a Waco appraisal or tax bill?
sections.html:
File for a homestead exemption if you live in the home, and protest the appraised value if the notice looks high. The appraisal district handles both, and the state deadline to file most exemption applications is before May 1.

McLennan CAD mails a notice of appraised value to owners whose market value rose at least $1,000 over the prior year. The notice lists market value, assessed value and taxable value. Market value is what the property would sell for on January 1. Assessed value reflects the homestead cap, and taxable value is what remains after exemptions.

  • Protest deadline: May 15, or 30 days after the notice is mailed, whichever is later.
  • Ways to file: by email, in person at 315 S 26th Street, or through the online portal, which the district opens for most residential property from April 10 through May 15.
  • After filing: an informal meeting with a district appraiser, and then a hearing before the appraisal review board if no settlement is reached.
  • Agents: a family member or friend can represent you if you file an appointment of agent form.

Evidence is posted in the online portal, which you reach with the property owner ID and PIN printed on the notice. The review board looks at market value, so bring sales of similar nearby homes and photos of condition problems. A homestead can also lock in a 10% annual cap on appraised value starting the year after the exemption is first granted, and owners 65 or older or disabled can freeze the school tax on that home.

sections.h2: What happens to Waco property tax if I sell?
sections.html:
The year's tax is secured by a lien from January 1, so it gets settled at closing. A title company pays the account from the seller's proceeds and prorates the rest.

Texas puts the liability on whoever owned the home on January 1, even if the sale closes later in the year, and a buyer cannot receive clear title while delinquent tax remains. A seller who is behind should request a statement from the tax office for the county, the city, the school district and the college. Inherited Waco homes follow the same rule: heirs who are not named on a recorded deed must give McLennan CAD an affidavit of ownership interest, the death certificate and a recent utility bill to claim the exemption.

Because about half of Waco's homes are renters, a seller with a tenant should also check whether a homestead exemption was ever filed. Rental property carries no homestead exemption, so the seller's bill may be higher than neighbors' bills on owner-occupied homes.

faqs.q: What is the Waco city property tax rate?
faqs.a: The City of Waco's rate is $0.755000 per $100 of taxable value for 2026, made up of $0.578371 for operations and $0.176629 for debt, according to the county's rate sheet. The city's adopted budget page says the rate stays at 75.5000 cents.

faqs.q: What is the Waco ISD homestead exemption?
faqs.a: McLennan County lists $140,000 as the general homestead exemption for Waco ISD, and $200,000 for owners 65 or older or disabled. The county's 2026 sheet shows Waco ISD at a total rate of 1.034870.

faqs.q: Is there a penalty for paying Waco property tax in February?
faqs.a: Yes. Taxes unpaid after January 31 are delinquent, and the collector adds a 6% penalty and 1% interest on February 1. The penalty climbs monthly to 12% by July 1.

faqs.q: Can I protest my McLennan County appraisal online?
faqs.a: Yes. McLennan CAD offers online filing for most residential property from April 10 to May 15, and the protest deadline is May 15 or 30 days after the notice is mailed, whichever is later.

faqs.q: Does a Waco rental house get a homestead exemption?
faqs.a: No. The exemption requires the owner to live in the home as a principal residence on January 1, and the owner cannot claim another residence homestead. A landlord's rental house is taxed without it.
